Referring to Figure Q.2:
- **Circuit Components:** A sinusoidal input $v_i$ with peak $\pm 15\text{ V}$, a series capacitor $C$, a parallel diode pointing upwards with a $5\text{ V}$ DC source, and a load resistor $R$.
- **Circuit Type:** This is a biased clamper (positive clamper with DC shift).
- **Analysis:**
  - During the negative half-cycle of $v_i$, the diode becomes forward-biased and conducts, charging the capacitor $C$.
  - Applying Kirchhoff's Voltage Law (KVL) across the diode branch: The output voltage is held at the reference level determined by the DC source and diode drop. With a $5\text{ V}$ source and assuming an ideal or silicon diode ($0.7\text{ V}$), the diode clamps the negative peak.
  - Specifically, the lower peak of the waveform is clamped to $-5\text{ V}$ (or $-5.7\text{ V}$ with diode drop).
- **Output Waveform:** The entire sinusoidal waveform is shifted upwards. The peak-to-peak value remains $30\text{ V}$ ($+15\text{ V}$ to $-15\text{ V}$), but it now ranges from a minimum of $-5\text{ V}$ to a maximum of $+25\text{ V}$.
proTip: Clampers shift the input waveform up or down without changing its peak-to-peak amplitude. The diode points in the direction of the shift.
